findings.title: Hung flusher processes are never killed before replacement
findings.body: Processes are created with multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, whose SpawnProcess class is not an instance of multiprocessing.Process (the default-context Process class) on Linux. The isinstance check therefore skips process.kill() for a hung flusher, after which _create_process_for_shards starts a replacement for the same shards. The hung and replacement processes can then concurrently flush the same Redis shards, racing flush/done_flush and potentially producing duplicate segments or interfering with each other's in-progress flushes.

findings.title: Flusher processes are not terminated in join() due to the same isinstance check
findings.body: As in the restart path, join() only calls process.terminate() when isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is true, which is false for SpawnProcess objects created from the spawn context on Linux. join() can therefore return while flusher processes are still running after the deadline; a subsequent rebalance/strategy for the same shards can run concurrently with these orphaned (until parent exit) flushers and duplicate work.

findings.title: --flusher-processes accepts zero and negative values without validation
findings.body: The new click option accepts any int. A negative value flows to SpanFlusher where min(negative, len(assigned_shards)) yields a negative num_processes and range() produces no processes at all: spans are written to Redis and offsets committed but nothing ever flushes them, with no error. A direct flusher_processes=0 via the factory is instead silently converted by `max_processes or len(...)` to one process per shard, the opposite of the requested limit. The option/factory should reject values < 1.

findings.title: Multi-process flusher test never verifies any segment is flushed
findings.body: test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts process counts and shard distribution, then joins; it submits no spans and asserts no produced output. The threaded produce_to_pipe path with multiple shards sharing processes, per-process restart/health bookkeeping, and the spawn-process path used in production are all unexercised, so regressions that drop or duplicate segments when shards share a flusher (or when a flusher restarts) would pass CI.
